County of Santa Clara
Social Services Agency
24-5577
DATE: May 7, 2024 (Item No. {{item.number}})
TO: Board of Supervisors
FROM: Daniel Little, Director, Social Services Agency
SUBJECT: Sourcewise - IHSS Career Pathways Program
RECOMMENDED ACTION
Approve Second Amendment to Agreement with Sourcewise relating to providing In-Home
Supportive Services Career Pathways Program increasing the maximum contract amount by
$444,855 from $233,708 to $678,563, with no change to the term of the agreement, that has
been reviewed and approved by County Counsel as to form and legality. A single source
exception to competitive procurement has been approved by the Office of Countywide
Contracting Management pursuant to Board of Supervisors Policy 5.6.5.1(D)(2)(a). (LA-1)
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS
There is no negative impact to the County General Fund as a result of the Recommended
Action.
The fiscal year (FY) 2023-2024 approved budget appropriation for the In-Home Supportive
Services (IHSS) Carrer Pathways Program is $194,400, with $194,400 in state revenues. The
Agency will submit a budget modification request for the difference of approved budget and
amended contract in the amount of $168,080 during FY 2023-2024 Year-end Budget Clean-
up process.
CONTRACT HISTORY
On December 29, 2022, the Procurement Department approved a single source exception to
Competitive Procurement pursuant to Board Policy 5.6.5.1 (D)(2)(a). The Single Source
recognized Sourcewise, Public Authority services provider, as the best-qualified organization
to provide training courses for eligible IHSS providers within the County.
On April 6, 2023, the Procurement Department approved the IHSS Career Pathways
retroactive contract with Sourcewise in the amount of $233,708 for the period October 1,
2022, through December 31, 2023.
On March 1, 2024, the Procurement Department approved the First Amendment to the IHSS
Career Pathways contract extending the contract term from December 31, 2023 to December
31, 2024.
Board of Supervisors: Sylvia Arenas, Cindy Chavez, Otto Lee, Susan Ellenberg, S. Joseph Simitian Page 1 of 3
County Executive: James R. Williams
REASONS FOR RECOMMENDATION AND BACKGROUND
The mission of SSA is to provide resources and opportunities in a culturally responsive
manner to enhance the quality of life in our community by protecting, educating, and
empowering individuals and families. In alignment with this mission, the IHSS Career
Pathways Program offers training opportunities designed to enhance the caregiving skills of
IHSS providers, thereby directly and positively benefiting the IHSS recipient. Offering this
program to the community supports the SSA Department of Aging and Adult Services
(DAAS) mission to help older adults, dependent adults, and the disabled live a safe and
independent lifestyle.
In 2021, Section 24 of California Senate Bill 172 added Welfare & Institutions Code Section
12316.1 and mandated the California Department of Social Services (CDSS) to develop and
administer the Career Pathways Pilot Program for providers of IHSS. $200 million was set
aside to fund the program through December 31, 2023. The goal of the program is to
incentivize, support, and fund career pathways for IHSS providers, allowing these workers to
build on their direct care experience and obtain positions such as certified home health aide,
certified nursing assistant, licensed vocational nurse, and more. Sourcewise is uniquely
qualified to provide these professional services due to their long-standing presence in the
community and extensive understanding of the administration of the IHSS Career Pathways
Program. IHSS providers who participate, and complete particular training modules receive a
payment incentive. These trainings are offered online, in person and in various languages and
locations throughout California. Many are held at the County’s IHSS building to maximize
the number of enrollees in Santa Clara County.
In 2023, CDSS granted an extension of funding for the IHSS Career Pathways Program
through December 31, 2024. Sourcewise fully utilized its entire state-reimbursed budget by
December 31, 2023. In response to the CDSS extension and based on the program’s success,
Sourcewise integrated additional classes. This Second Amendment is set to provide
approximately 738 3-hour training classes for IHSS providers and the active participation in
the program indicates a significant need for training opportunities designed to enhance
provider skills through payment incentives.
In accordance with Board of Supervisors (Board) Policy 5.3.5.1, the Board is the only body
that has the authority to enter into contracts and issue solicitations on behalf of the County,
unless the contracting authority has been delegated explicitly to someone other than the
Board pursuant to state law, County Ordinance Code, resolution, or express action of the
Board.
CHILD IMPACT
The recommended action will have no/neutral impact on children and youth.
SENIOR IMPACT
The recommended action will have a positive impact on seniors by providing current training
to IHSS caregivers resulting in enhanced, higher quality care for IHSS recipients and serving
as a viable alternative to out-of-home care.
Board of Supervisors: Sylvia Arenas, Cindy Chavez, Otto Lee, Susan Ellenberg, S. Joseph Simitian Page 2 of 3
County Executive: James R. Williams
Agenda Date: May 7, 2024
SUSTAINABILITY IMPLICATIONS
The recommended action will have no/neutral sustainability implications.
CONSEQUENCES OF NEGATIVE ACTION
SSA will not implement the IHSS Career Pathways Program, which will restrict services to
IHSS providers in the County.
STEPS FOLLOWING APPROVAL
Upon approval, the Clerk of the Board is requested to notify Jorge Montes, Alana Rainville,
Crystal Chavez, and Patrice Robles from SSA.

1. SCOPE OF WORK
CONTRACTOR will provide the Career Pathways Program for providers of IHSS and Waiver
Personal Care Services (WPCS) to increase the quality of care, recruitment, and retention of
providers of services for recipients of IHSS and to provide training opportunities for career
advancement in the home care and health care industries.

information from CDSS for program reimbursement and as outlined in Section 6 of this
Exhibit. Invoices must be signed by the CONTRACTOR.
b. SSA Outcome Measurement Reporting
CONTRACTOR will submit a quarterly report as outlined in Section 7 of this Exhibit and
Exhibit D-1: Work Plan Logic Model.

The term begins on October 1, 2022 and expires on December 31, 2024, unless terminated
earlier or otherwise amended.

provisions of this Contract, for a total not to exceed $118,395 for period October 1, 2023
through June 30, 2023, and $115,313 for period July 1, 2023 through December 31, 2024, for
a total of $233,708.
5. BUDGET CONTINGENCY
This Contract is contingent upon the appropriation of sufficient funding by the County for the
services covered by this Contract. Notwithstanding the termination provisions set forth herein,

RECOMMENDED ACTION
Approve Agreement with Exemplar Human Services, LLC, relating to providing reporting
tools and services in an amount not to exceed $595,000 for period February 6, 2024 through
June 30, 2025, that has been reviewed and approved by County Counsel as to form and
legality. A sole source exception to competitive procurement has been approved by the
Office of Countywide Contracting Management pursuant to Board of Supervisors Policy
5.6.5.1(D)(2)(a). (LA-1)
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS
There is no negative impact to the County General Fund as a result of the Recommended
Action.
The cost of $595,000 for the Agreement with Exemplar Human Services LLC, for the period
of February 6, 2024, through June 30, 2025, is included in the Agency’s Fiscal Year 2023-
2024 Adopted Budget. No additional appropriation is needed.
REASONS FOR RECOMMENDATION AND BACKGROUND
The mission of the Social Services Agency is to provide resources and opportunities in a
culturally responsive manner to enhance the quality of life in our community by protecting,
educating, and empowering individuals and families. In alignment with this mission, services
related to Reporting Tools and Services by Exemplar Human Services, LLC will provide
staff in the Department of Employment and Benefit Services (DEBS) with a portfolio of
reporting tools to assist staff in meeting CalSAWS service and performance outcomes.
Reason(s) for approval:
In accordance with the Board’s Chapter 5 Policy, section 5.3.5.1, the Board is the only body
that has authority to enter into contracts and issue solicitations on behalf of the County,
unless contracting authority has been specifically delegated to someone other than the Board
pursuant to state law, County Ordinance Code, resolution, or express action of the Board.
The California Statewide Automated Welfare System (CalSAWS) is the automated welfare
business process in California that was to be implemented by all 58 counties in 2023. The
Board of Supervisors: Sylvia Arenas, Cindy Chavez, Otto Lee, Susan Ellenberg, S. Joseph Simitian Page 1 of 2
County Executive: James R. Williams
implementation of CalSAWS will merge California’s most recent three county-level
consortia welfare systems and will support six core programs: California Work Opportunity
and Responsibility to Kids (CalWORKs), Supplemental Nutritional Assistance Program
(SNAP) known as CalFresh in California, Medi-Cal, Foster Care, Refugee Assistance, and
County Medical Services. It encompasses the following functions: eligibility determination,
benefit computation, benefit delivery, case management and information management.
With the transition to CalSAWS, DEBS requires productivity reports to assist staff and
management in maximizing daily operations and processing of tasks. Exemplar creates
reports customized for each individual staff member assisting in managing and maintaining
productivity to meet state mandates.
CHILD IMPACT
The recommended action will have no/neutral impact on children and youth.
SENIOR IMPACT
The recommended action will have no/neutral impact on seniors.
SUSTAINABILITY IMPLICATIONS
The recommended action will have no/neutral sustainability implications.
CONSEQUENCES OF NEGATIVE ACTION
The contract with Exemplar Human Services, LLC for Reporting Tools and Services will not
be executed, which would result in DEBS not being able to obtain reports needed to
maximize CalSAWS daily operations.
STEPS FOLLOWING APPROVAL
Upon approval, the Clerk of the Board is requested to notify Jorge Montes, Alana Rainville,
Chad Keele, and Jennifer Nhem from the SSA.

County of Santa Clara
Behavioral Health Services Department
23-1733
DATE: January 23, 2024 (Item No. {{item.number}})
TO: Board of Supervisors
FROM: Sherri Terao, Director, Behavioral Health Services Department
SUBJECT: Agreement with Abode Services
RECOMMENDED ACTION
Approve retroactive Agreement with Abode Services relating to providing rent
administration and payment services in an amount not to exceed $3,900,000 for period
January 1, 2024 through June 30, 2024, that has been reviewed and approved by County
Counsel as to form and legality. A single source exception to competitive procurement has
been approved by the Office of Countywide Contracting Management pursuant to Board of
Supervisors Policy 5.6.5.1(D)(2)(a).
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS
Approval of the recommended action would have no net impact on the County General Fund.
Services under this Agreement are funded through the Mental Health Services Act (MHSA)
and are included in the Behavioral Health Services Department’s (BHSD) Fiscal Year (FY)
2023-2024 Adopted Budget. BHSD is contracting with Abode Services (Abode) for
$3,900,000, of which 93% would be direct financial assistance for adults and older adults
who are enrolled in mental health outpatient treatment and receiving intensive services.
CONTRACT HISTORY
The Agreement with Abode is a new contract. On November 13, 2023, the Office of
Countywide Contracting Management (OCCM) approved a single source exception to
competitive procurement for the contract with Abode.
REASONS FOR RECOMMENDATION AND BACKGROUND
The recommended action would approve an Agreement with Abode to serve as the
administrator of rent payments and other financial assistance (e.g., security deposits to
establish placement, one-time repairs for property damage, and monthly family financial
support) for adults and older adults who are currently enrolled in intensive services or need to
transition to a different level of care.
Board of Supervisors: Sylvia Arenas, Cindy Chavez, Otto Lee, Susan Ellenberg, S. Joseph Simitian Page 1 of 3
County Executive: James R. Williams
Under the Agreement, Abode would administer rental subsidy payments and other housing-
related financial assistance. Currently, housing funds are administered by each County
Contracted Provider (CCP) for the clients in their care. When clients transition to another
provider or level of care, the housing funds stay with the CCP and do not follow the client,
which could disrupt their housing stability. Housing funds administered by Abode would
follow the client through the system, regardless of provider or level of care. allowing clients
to transition seamlessly from intensive services to other necessary outpatient programs
without causing delays or disruptions to housing payments.
Justification for Retroactive Start Date
BHSD is seeking the Board of Supervisors’ approval of this Agreement at the earliest
opportunity. After six months of evaluation and planning, BHSD, CCPs, and stakeholders
agreed to change the way rental assistance is provided to individuals receiving intensive
services. Abode was chosen due to their knowledge and expertise in timely rent
administration to housing operators for clients in multiple IOP programs. In addition, they
possess extensive experience working with other County Departments such as the Office of
Supportive Housing and are familiar with County processes. Lastly, Abode currently
provides a full array of wrap-around resident services to dozens of permanent supportive
housing communities in the Bay Area and has a long working history with local providers. A
retroactive start date of January 1, 2024 is requested to prevent disruptions to clients’ housing
placement.
Abode’s services would include, but are not limited to, rental subsidy payments and other
housing-related financial assistance such as security deposit assistance, utility deposits, and
one-time payments for damages. Abode, being the single administrator of housing funds,
would allow for rent payments to be made in a timely manner. Abode would communicate
with CCPs, when applicable, on matters such as subsidy changes, and would mutually
address issues related to compliance with lease and other housing-related matters. Clients
shall be able to move into housing with zero income to reduce the amount of time they
remain unhoused. This program reduces placement disruption by ensuring rent payments are
made in a timely manner, thus reducing the probability of displacement.
Housing stability promotes resiliency and recovery for individuals living with behavioral
health conditions. Lack of stable housing can lead to distress, negatively impact mental and
emotional health, and exacerbate symptoms. A streamlined administrator who provides rent
administration and payment services, will enable clients to transition seamlessly from one
program to another without putting them at risk of homelessness.
CHILD IMPACT
The recommended action will have no/neutral impact on children and youth.
Board of Supervisors: Sylvia Arenas, Cindy Chavez, Otto Lee, Susan Ellenberg, S. Joseph Simitian Page 2 of 3
County Executive: James R. Williams
Agenda Date: January 23, 2024
SENIOR IMPACT
The recommended action would positively impact seniors by allowing older adults to
transition seamlessly from IOP services to other necessary outpatient programs without
causing disruptions to clients’ housing payments.
SUSTAINABILITY IMPLICATIONS
The recommended action balances public policy and program interests and enhances the
Board of Supervisors’ sustainability goals of social equity and safety by providing
streamlined financial assistance to help adults and older adults obtain and maintain stable
housing placements.
CONSEQUENCES OF NEGATIVE ACTION
Failure to approve the recommended action would result in delayed housing supports to
impacted adults and older adults, who are receiving IOP services or are ready to transition to
a lower level of care, and in need of housing placements.
STEPS FOLLOWING APPROVAL
Priority processing is requested for this Agreement to ensure rent payments are administered
for timely placements. Upon approval, the Clerk of the Board is requested to send e-mail
notifications to ShuNing Liang (ShuNing.Liang@hhs.sccgov.org), Sabry Ramirez
(Sabry.Ramirez@hhs.sccgov.org), Angeleah Macatiag
(Angeleah.Macatiag@hhs.sccgov.org), Tiffanie Johnson (Tiffanie.Johnson@hhs.sccgov.org),
Evonne Lai (Evonne.Lai@hhs.sccgov.org), and Earl Ong (Earl.Ong@hhs.sccgov.org).

ability to achieve timeliness of rent administration services with forty-eight (48) hour turnaround for rent checks
and be able to coordinate with the BHSD Program Manager and County-Contracted Providers (CCPs) to
